hypothesis: Established HMMER profile construction and full-sequence scoring may adjudicate a bounded set of ambiguous family-profile matches better than OrthoHMM's approximate profile scorer. A family-HMM match is homology evidence, not an orthology call. No positive result is assumed.
baseline: Frozen canonical high_sensitivity/satellite_v2 OrthoHMM, initial min4/cap100, BLOSUM62, CPM0.1/seed4, one original unweighted profile pass, default refinement, inferred min_variance species tree and species_overlap/positive_paralogy reconciliation with legacy support mapping. Custom profile weighting, global alignment guard, local joint-tree rescue and all other new mechanisms remain off.
candidate_generation: Use the unmodified in-memory original profile-source clusters, built-in significant profile-hit table, minimum member self-score thresholds, complete FASTA/gene ownership and authenticated initial sequence-HMM hits from the same baseline profile pass. No new prefilter, global database expansion, benchmark labels, comparator predictions or GO/EC/FAS annotations enter inference.

For each query, collect all significant built-in external family-profile hits, excluding its own source family. Deduplicate repeated query/profile rows by their maximum raw score. Retain every such competing profile, including a profile lacking an initial sequence anchor: it can block recruitment but cannot create a graph edge without sequence support.

A query is ambiguous if it has multiple external profiles, or if it has one external profile whose raw score is below that profile's original minimum member self-score. Require at least one external family with positive existing initial sequence-HMM support in either direction. Preserve the baseline's original per-family sequence-anchor choice, highest positive score and member-order tie rule.

If a query has more than four significant external profiles, exclude the entire query from this intervention; do not truncate its competition. Add its own source-family profile as a competitor whenever that original profile exists. There are at most five complete competitors per query. No new profile is invented for an unprofiled singleton or small own family; report those cases explicitly.

Rank eligible queries by absolute(raw_best_external_score - its_original_self_threshold)/max(1,abs(original_self_threshold)), nearest boundary first, then canonical gene name. When the best raw external score ties, use canonical sorted source-member tuples only to choose the descriptive threshold for this priority calculation, not to select an assignment. The fixed query list is identical across all active arms.

Walk that ranking once, selecting at most128 queries and at most128 distinct source profiles. If accepting an entire query would exceed the profile budget, leave that query unchanged and record the exclusion; never drop a competitor to fit the budget. No second round, transitive expansion, family union or post-result budget sweep.

Archive all eligibility, ambiguity, source ownership, anchor, priority and budget decisions, including excluded/unexamined queries, complete competitor lists, original strict-profile decisions and a canonical candidate-list digest. Candidate generation must be identical across builtin_reselect, hmmer_score_only and hmmer_reselect.
profile_and_scoring_controls: For each selected source family, reconstruct the same center-star alignment from the same native encoded sequences, original member order, original unchanged CPU alignment library, BLOSUM62 and gap-open/extension settings. Verify that recomputing the original unweighted PSSM reproduces the stored original match emissions/consensus/transition parameters before using this alignment. Save the source alignment and the original known-residue match-column mask.

Write a tokenized Stockholm alignment with RF columns matching that native unweighted mask. Build a standard HMMER3.4 profile using hmmbuild --amino --hand --wnone --enone --seed 42 --cpu 0, a deterministic model name and -O to retain HMMER's annotated source alignment. These explicit unweighted/actual-count construction controls keep the earlier weighting intervention off. HMMER's mixture priors, position-specific transitions and scoring remain standard implementation behavior; this is not HMMER's default weighting configuration or a numerically identical native model.

Use each profile only on its complete original source members for self-score calibration and the selected queries that list it as a competitor. Deduplicate the union of these targets. Every query is scored against every listed competitor, including its own original profile when available. Other queried targets or incidental file records must not become candidates for recruitment.

Run hmmsearch --max --seed 42 --cpu 0 --noali with per-target and per-domain tables, broad score reporting thresholds -T -1000000000 and --domT -1000000000, and -Z equal to the full original proteome collection's gene count, not the selected target count. Keep the null2 composition correction enabled. --max disables heuristic filters for this bounded validation; its cost must be reported. Each external build/search invocation has a600-second timeout; a timeout is a preserved tool failure, not a missing measurement or an inactivity fallback.

Use only the full-sequence table's HMMER bit score and sequence E-value for decisions. Retain best-domain scores, biases, domain coordinates and conditional/independent domain E-values as diagnostics, never as a new coverage gate or orthology probability. Conditional domain values refer to HMMER's reported target subset and are not substituted for full-database sequence E-values.

Decision values are the CLI table's reported precision. HMMER bit-score ties at printed precision abstain; do not claim these are exact latent-score ties. A reported sequence E-value equal to1e-4 fails the strict gate. Do not convert the built-in normalized initial-hit scores or raw integer profile scores into claimed HMMER bit scores.

Require a complete successful tool exit, standard completed table footer, exact model/token identity, valid finite scores/E-values, unique target rows and no unexpected targets. Preserve commands, environment, versions, binary hashes, mappings, alignments, model files, raw tables and stderr. Malformed/truncated output is a failure, not a negative hit.

A genuinely unreported query/competitor or source member is an explicit missing measurement, not an invented zero or minus-infinity score. Do not silently drop the competitor or member: preserve that selected query's legacy profile decision if any required competitor/calibration measurement is missing. Report incomplete-measurement abstention separately from a complete scored rejection.

For builtin_reselect, score the exact same competitor/query and all source-member sets with the existing original CPU profile scorer at band64. Verify that recomputed minimum member scores match the original self thresholds. Use the unchanged approximate BLOSUM62 significance rule with the complete proteome residue count. Keep approximation versus HMMER calibration limitations explicit.
decision_rule: off executes the existing baseline exactly, with no selection, HMMER calls or decision changes.

hmmer_score_only constructs and scores the frozen selected comparisons, records all counterfactual decisions, and returns the exact original strict-profile edges unchanged. Verify byte-identical graph/candidate/native products and matching scores versus off before interpreting any active HMMER result.

builtin_reselect and hmmer_reselect apply the same fixed replacement rule only to the frozen selected queries, using their respective backend scores, significance and minimum complete-source-member self-score. Other queries and all initial sequence-hit edges are unchanged.

For a completely measured selected query, find the unique highest raw-profile-score (builtin) or reported full-sequence bit-score (HMMER) across all listed competitors before applying acceptance gates. Do not skip a higher-scoring failed competitor in favor of a weaker passing family. A top-score tie, own-family winner, failing sequence E-value, score below that winning family's minimum member self-score, or missing positive initial sequence anchor yields no strict-profile edge for this selected query. These complete-data rejections replace any legacy strict-profile edge for this query; incomplete measurements instead preserve its legacy edge.

An external unique winner must have strict sequence E<1e-4, score>=its backend's minimum member self-score and an existing positive initial sequence-HMM anchor in that original family. Emit only that anchor link, weighted by the unchanged original initial sequence-hit score, not a new HMMER score scale.

Pass resulting profile edges through unchanged ordinary graph clustering/refinement, satellite_v2 candidate construction and native inferred-species-tree/reconciliation writers. Do not append native pairs, change membership constraints, or equate the profile winner with an orthology call. Independent graph/singleton steps can retain/reintroduce links; report final effects rather than claiming all rejected links globally disappear.
ablation_interpretation: off versus hmmer_score_only tests that measurement/provenance alone does not alter inference.
off versus builtin_reselect measures the replacement-decision policy with the original scoring backend.

builtin_reselect versus hmmer_reselect holds nomination and the decision form fixed while changing the controlled HMM construction/scoring/significance backend. It does not isolate emission priors, position-specific transitions, null correction and significance calibration from each other; acknowledge those remaining bundled effects.

No candidate-generation gain can be claimed: the candidate universe is deliberately fixed. Compare actual selected/rejected/rescued/reassigned counts, source/member support and final groups/pairs separately. HMMER's utility is not established by a gain that is fully explained by builtin_reselect.
evaluation: Test fixed candidate selection, complete competitor/own-family handling, unanchored blockers, exact/printed ties, ranking and input-order invariance, all budgets, invalid ownership and empty/inactive cases. Test genuine HMMER3.4 model building/search, native PSSM reconstruction, full-database -Z behavior, source-member calibration, token/coordinate/score parsing, missing measurements, malformed tables, tool failures and fresh artifact preservation.
Require nonempty real synthetic backend/decision fixtures and ordinary final native integration. Unit or synthetic results are not biological accuracy or generalizability evidence.

Before accuracy interpretation, probe actual applicability on complete OrthoBench. If no query can be completely measured, try corrected QfO then Three Kingdoms in that fixed order without retuning. Tool failures do not count as inactivity or justify fallback. Zero changed decisions must be reported explicitly rather than manufactured into an active accuracy comparison.

Run the four prespecified OrthoBench arms with an exact unchanged off control and exact hmmer_score_only control, independently validating activation, full unique ownership, graph/candidate/native products and official OG precision/recall/F1. Report native-pair turnover separately from OG F1.

An active reselect arm advances only if its OG F1 strictly exceeds off and neither precision nor recall drops by more than0.005. Apply the gate to each arm independently; do not choose only the largest observed gain. Stop failed fixed branches without retuning. A HMMER-specific benefit additionally requires a favorable comparison with the decision-only builtin_reselect arm, with appropriate uncertainty/limitations.

Execute unchanged advancing settings on complete corrected QfO and Three Kingdoms, reporting all eight endpoint slots, precision/recall/coverage/evaluated populations, resources and defensible uncertainty. Unrun endpoints stay NA. Existing panels remain development-exposed, TreeFam supporting and Three Kingdoms supplementary; post-freeze independent confirmation is desirable but its absence limits claims rather than blocking completion.
implementation_scope: Implement reusable label-independent selection/scoring/decision functions in the OrthoHMM package and explicit experimental profile-replay/pilot integration first. Keep default production behavior unchanged. Complete a tested production opt-in interface and full-vector confirmation if promising; a bounded negative prototype remains clearly experimental.

resources.timing: Separate original profile replay, selection, native rescoring, HMMER building/scoring and final native costs; shared-host descriptive incremental wall/CPU/max-process-RSS, not isolated full-pipeline runtime or aggregate process-tree memory.

documentation.scope: Primary HMMER documentation for full-sequence versus domain reporting, -Z target-count scaling, --max, null2 correction, seed and worker/master thread semantics. Exact installed3.4 help/man/source and binary versions will be pinned; no claim that upstream master is the executed release.

Primary HMMER documentation for explicit amino alphabet, Stockholm reference columns, uniform relative weights, actual effective count and retained annotated alignment. These are controlled standard-tool options, not default HMMER weighting or a validated orthology model.
Existing local HMMER3.4 source/manual/binaries; inspect and authenticate before execution rather than installing an unrelated backend or silently using another version.

git: Commit and push this protocol before implementation/evaluation, then focused tested package/replay/pilot milestones, immutable manifests and result/readback decisions. Preserve all existing running/queued scientific source trees, failures and unrelated user work.
